analysis.title: "One Trick Pony": JPM Strategy Chair On America's (Over)-Reliance On AI
key_insights: A basket of 42 AI stocks accounts for 60%-80% of S&P 500 earnings growth, price returns and capital spending since Jan 2024.
60% of S&P 500 stocks are down 20% or more from their all-time highs, even though the index is close to its all-time high.
Only 30% of stocks are outperforming the S&P 500, one of the lowest readings since 1991.
AI is benefiting AI supply chain companies more than the companies adopting it.
Technology's share of US GDP growth has risen from almost zero through 2022 to about 33%.
Only 20% of US states are growing faster than the national average, almost the lowest since 1979.

AI is the only positive trend in US construction spending, up 38% since January 2024. Manufacturing (-28%), commercial real estate (-13%) and residential (-6%) construction are all down over the same period.
The decline in planned data centers is flagged as something to watch, since data center construction is the only growing construction category.

Tech multiples are not cheap, but since January 2024 global tech stocks have mostly been driven by earnings growth rather than P/E multiple expansion. Cembalest notes markets driven by earnings growth are in his experience less prone to rapid declines than those driven mostly by multiples.

Cembalest expresses foreboding about the SpaceX IPO given the track record of other large IPOs since 2010 as lockup expirations approached. SpaceX is holding up better than most after 116 days, but only about 20% of its shares have been released into the free float, so it may be too early to judge.

sector_views.rationale: Tech multiples are not cheap, but returns since Jan 2024 have come mostly from earnings growth rather than multiple expansion. The economy and market are heavily concentrated in AI.

earnings_insights: A basket of 42 AI stocks accounts for 60%-80% of S&P 500 earnings growth since Jan 2024.
Global tech returns since Jan 2024 have been driven mostly by earnings growth rather than P/E multiple expansion.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Almost the lowest since 1979, which points to narrow regional growth.

risk_factors: Concentration of S&P earnings growth, returns and capex in 42 AI stocks.
A decline in planned data centers would hit the only growing US construction category.
Large IPO lockup expirations, with the SpaceX IPO as the example. About 20% of its shares are in the free float so far.
Narrow market breadth and narrow regional growth.

60% of S&P 500 stocks are down 20% or more from all-time highs while the index sits near its own high.

tension_points.bear_case: A basket of 42 AI stocks drives 60%-80% of S&P earnings growth, returns and capex, while 60% of S&P stocks are down 20% or more from highs and breadth is among the weakest since 1991.
